Remote-Sensing Bayesian Models

remote-sensing-models-1.3.Rd

Version 1.3.0 tools for analysis-ready UAV, satellite, proximal-sensor and field-phenotyping data. The module keeps image preprocessing separate from Bayesian modeling, supports optional terra/sf extraction, common vegetation indices, calibration, spatial and temporal models, known predictor measurement errors, multi-sensor fusion, posterior prediction, map-ready uncertainty products, and change analysis.

bayes_rs_data(x, x_coord = NULL, y_coord = NULL, time = NULL, id = NULL,
  source = "unknown", metadata = list(), na.rm = FALSE)

bayes_rs_extract(raster, locations, x_coord = NULL, y_coord = NULL,
  id = NULL, fun = c("mean", "median", "min", "max", "sum"),
  method = c("simple", "bilinear"), exact = FALSE, na.rm = TRUE)

bayes_rs_indices(data, nir, red, blue = NULL, green = NULL,
  red_edge = NULL, indices = c("NDVI", "EVI", "SAVI", "NDRE"),
  L = 0.5, prefix = "rs_")

bayes_rs_calibrate(data, reference, sensor, group = NULL,
  draws = 2000L, seed = 20260826)

bayes_rs_model(data, response, predictors, fixed = NULL,
  x_coord = NULL, y_coord = NULL, time = NULL, subject = NULL,
  block = NULL, group = NULL, predictor_sd = NULL,
  family = c("gaussian", "student"), spatial = NULL,
  temporal = c("none", "ar1", "factor", "linear"),
  spatial_cov = c("exp_quad", "matern32", "matern52", "exponential"),
  k = NULL, scale = TRUE)

bayes_rs_fusion(data, response, sources, predictor_sd = NULL, ...)
bayes_rs_phenotype(data, trait, features, ...)
bayes_rs_predict(fit, newdata = NULL, type = c("mean", "predictive"),
  level = 0.95, re_formula = NA, ndraws = NULL)
bayes_rs_uncertainty(prediction, threshold = NULL,
  direction = c("above", "below"))
bayes_rs_map(prediction, x_coord = NULL, y_coord = NULL,
  quantity = c("mean", "median", "lower", "upper", "posterior_sd", "interval_width"),
  as_raster = FALSE, crs = NULL)
bayes_rs_change(fit, newdata, baseline_time, comparison_time,
  threshold = 0, level = 0.95)

Arguments

x, data

A data frame, bayes_rs_data, or optional terra::SpatRaster, as documented by each function.

x_coord, y_coord

Coordinate column names. They are required only for explicitly spatial operations.

time

Optional acquisition-time column. Numeric, Date, and POSIX time are supported by the data/model constructors.

id

Optional plot, pixel, sampling-unit, or extraction identifier.

source

Short provenance label such as "uav", "satellite", "proximal", or "ground".

metadata

Named provenance list.

na.rm

Whether missing raster values are removed in the relevant extraction/conversion operation.

raster

A terra::SpatRaster; terra is optional.

locations

Point/polygon locations supplied as a matrix, data frame, optional sf object, or terra::SpatVector.

fun

Polygon extraction summary.

method

Point extraction method, "simple" or "bilinear".

exact

Whether exact polygon-cell fractions are requested from terra.

nir, red, blue, green, red_edge

Band names. Blue is required for EVI and red edge for NDRE.

indices

Requested vegetation indices among NDVI, EVI, SAVI, and NDRE.

L

SAVI soil-adjustment constant.

prefix

Prefix for derived index column/layer names.

reference, sensor

Reference and sensor variables used for calibration.

group

Optional calibration or model grouping variable(s), depending on the function.

draws

Number of approximate coefficient draws for lightweight calibration.

seed

Reproducibility seed.

response, trait

Scientific response or phenotyping trait.

predictors, features

Numeric remote-sensing predictors.

fixed

Optional additional fixed-effect specification.

subject

Optional repeated-series identifier for AR(1).

block

Optional experimental block.

predictor_sd

Named mapping from error-prone predictors to columns containing known positive standard errors.

family

Gaussian or Student-t response family.

spatial

Whether to include a two-dimensional Gaussian-process term.

temporal

Temporal structure: none, AR(1), factor, or linear.

spatial_cov

Gaussian-process covariance kernel.

k

Optional approximate GP basis size.

scale

Whether coordinates are scaled inside the GP term.

sources

Named list mapping sensor/source labels to predictor columns.

...

Additional arguments passed through a wrapper or print/predict method.

fit

A fitted remote-sensing bayes_fit.

newdata

Optional prediction data.

type

Posterior mean or posterior predictive observations.

level

Credible interval mass.

re_formula

Group-level effect specification passed to the common prediction layer.

ndraws

Optional number of retained posterior draws.

prediction

Posterior prediction object containing draws and summaries.

threshold

Optional scientific threshold.

direction

Posterior probability above or below the threshold.

quantity

Posterior quantity formatted for mapping.

as_raster

Whether to request an optional terra raster rather than a map-ready data frame.

crs

Optional CRS used when rasterizing a regular prediction grid.

baseline_time, comparison_time

Two acquisition times used for posterior change.

Details

Remote-sensing products are treated as measurements rather than error-free truth. When standard-error columns are supplied through predictor_sd, the brms route creates explicit latent predictor submodels using mi(). Raster and sf interoperability are optional capabilities; no heavy dependency is installed automatically.

Value

Objects vary by function: analysis-ready data, extraction tables, vegetation indices, calibration objects, remote-sensing bayes_design objects, posterior prediction summaries, uncertainty tables, map-ready products, or posterior change summaries.

Examples

# 1. analysis-ready data: three usage patterns
d <- bayes_teaching_data("uav")
rs <- bayes_rs_data(d, "x", "y", id = "plot_id", source = "uav")
rs2 <- bayes_rs_data(d, "x", "y", source = "proximal")
sat <- bayes_rs_data(bayes_teaching_data("satellite"), "x", "y", time = "day")

# 2. explicit optional raster extraction: three support/method examples
if (FALSE) bayes_rs_extract(r, d, "x", "y", id = "plot_id")
if (FALSE) bayes_rs_extract(r, points, method = "bilinear")
if (FALSE) bayes_rs_extract(r, polygons, fun = "mean", exact = TRUE)

# 3. vegetation indices: three examples
z <- bayes_rs_indices(d, "nir", "red", blue = "blue", red_edge = "red_edge")
ndvi <- bayes_rs_indices(d, "nir", "red", indices = "NDVI")
savi <- bayes_rs_indices(d, "nir", "red", indices = "SAVI", L = 0.5)

# 4. lightweight sensor calibration: three examples
c <- bayes_teaching_data("rs_calibration")
cal <- bayes_rs_calibrate(c, "ground_biomass", "uav_biomass", draws = 200)
cal2 <- bayes_rs_calibrate(c, "ground_biomass", "uav_biomass", group = "platform", draws = 200)
cal3 <- bayes_rs_calibrate(c, "ground_biomass", "uav_biomass", draws = 100, seed = 1)

# 5. remote-sensing models: three examples
des <- bayes_rs_model(z, "biomass", c("rs_ndvi", "canopy_height"), x_coord = "x", y_coord = "y", block = "block")
des_simple <- bayes_rs_model(d, "biomass", "ndvi", spatial = FALSE)
des_me <- bayes_rs_model(d, "biomass", "ndvi", predictor_sd = c(ndvi = "ndvi_se"), spatial = FALSE)

# 6. multi-sensor fusion: three examples
f <- bayes_teaching_data("sensor_fusion")
fus <- bayes_rs_fusion(f, "biomass", list(uav = c("uav_ndvi", "height"), satellite = "sat_ndvi"), x_coord = "x", y_coord = "y")
fus2 <- bayes_rs_fusion(f, "biomass", list(uav = "uav_ndvi", proximal = "soil_moisture"), spatial = FALSE)
fus3 <- bayes_rs_fusion(f, "biomass", list(uav = "uav_ndvi", satellite = "sat_ndvi"), predictor_sd = c(uav_ndvi = "uav_ndvi_se", sat_ndvi = "sat_ndvi_se"), spatial = FALSE)

# 7. phenotyping wrapper: three examples
ph <- bayes_rs_phenotype(d, "biomass", c("ndvi", "canopy_height"), x_coord = "x", y_coord = "y")
ph2 <- bayes_rs_phenotype(d, "biomass", "ndvi", spatial = FALSE)
ph3 <- bayes_rs_phenotype(d, "biomass", "ndre", block = "block", spatial = FALSE)

# Heavy posterior examples require an explicitly configured backend.
if (FALSE) {
  pred1 <- bayes_rs_predict(rs_fit)
  pred2 <- bayes_rs_predict(rs_fit, future_pixels)
  pred3 <- bayes_rs_predict(rs_fit, type = "predictive")

  unc1 <- bayes_rs_uncertainty(pred1)
  unc2 <- bayes_rs_uncertainty(pred1, threshold = 5, direction = "above")
  unc3 <- bayes_rs_uncertainty(pred1, threshold = 3, direction = "below")

  map1 <- bayes_rs_map(pred1, quantity = "mean")
  map2 <- bayes_rs_map(pred1, quantity = "posterior_sd")
  map3 <- bayes_rs_map(pred1, quantity = "mean", as_raster = TRUE)

  ch1 <- bayes_rs_change(rs_fit, grid, 0, 28, threshold = 0)
  ch2 <- bayes_rs_change(rs_fit, grid, 14, 28, threshold = 0.5)
  ch3 <- bayes_rs_change(rs_fit, grid, 0, 14, threshold = -0.2)
}
